text: $SAND surged 44.6% to $0.06465, trading a wide range from $0.04427 up to $0.0735 and raking in almost $60 M of USDT volume. Meanwhile $QNT slipped 8.2% to $229.9, its low stuck at $223.51 after hitting $261.87 earlier, still pulling roughly $78 M in volume. On the middle-ground, $AAVE nudged up 5.6% to $180.82, bouncing between $170.64 and $187.5 with about $60 M traded. Big gainers are pulling ahead while the heavyweight loser is dragging its feet. Looks like the market's split between a few sharp moves and a lot of sideways action.

$QNT slipped to $246.94, its 24-hour swing only 23.2% versus the usual 38.4%, that's about a third tighter than normal.

$NEAR's at $4.856 after drifting down 4.99%; the day's range was 8.1% compared with a typical 12.9%, so it's also roughly a third tighter.

$SUI nudged up to $1.1754, up 0.65%; it moved within a 7.8% band versus the average 10% swing, again a bit tighter than usual.

All three are just a little more constrained today, no big moves beyond that.

$ETH is shedding ground against $BTC, down about 1.24% in the pair. Meanwhile $BTC climbed roughly 1.96% over the last 24 hours. The 20-coin basket of top alts slipped about 1.61% on average, so $BTC is beating the whole alt set. $ETH's relative weakness versus $BTC lines up with the broader alt sell-off. Nothing wild, just $BTC pulling ahead while $ETH lags behind.

$BTC closed at $84,750, up 1.211 % on the day. It hit a high of $85,273.65 before slipping to a low of $83,186, trading about 16,923 BTC with $1.42 B in USDT volume.

$ETH nudged higher, finishing at $2,701.53 (+0.6 %). The pair bounced between $2,673.13 and $2,722, moving roughly 264,705 ETH and $712.8 M in USDT volume.

$BNB ticked up to $771.29 (+0.507 %). Its range was tight, $763.02 low, $774.48 high, with 94,096 BNB traded and $72.36 M USDT changing hands.

Watch the USDT-quoted volume on $BTC; the surge past $1.4 B could signal tighter liquidity as price edges higher.

$MOVR exploded, price jumping to $2.99 and swinging about 2½ times its usual daily range, a 52% spread in 24 hrs.

$BTC barely budged on the overall chart, but its 2.9% range was still about 35% wider than the norm, nudging the 84,972 USDT level up by a hair.

That's the whole story, one token went ballistic, the other just a bit more active than usual.

$MOVR surged 89.3% to $2.425, hitting a high of $2.493 after bouncing from a low near $1.25. Volume spiked past 66 M USDT, showing real appetite. Meanwhile $SOL slipped 0.8% to $118.56, trading between $117.06 and $122.83 with about 348 M USDT changing hands. One token rocketing, the other barely sliding, the 24-hour spread is pretty clear. Nothing wild beyond that; just $MOVR pulling ahead while $SOL drags its heels.

$SUI's been moving in a narrow band, the 24-hour swing was about 6.4%, roughly a third tighter than its usual 11% range. Price nudged up a hair, ending at $1.1579 with a 0.3% gain.

$XRP kept the same vibe, trading between $1.48 and $1.49. Its daily range sat at 4%, about half of the typical 6.3% swing, and it slipped 0.5% to finish at $1.4879.

Both tokens looked a lot calmer than normal, just holding steady without any wild moves. Nothing crazy on the chart, just a smooth ride.

$BTC up about 1.33% in the last 24 h, but the top-20 alt basket is screaming higher, roughly 7.3% gain. $ETH is slipping against Bitcoin, down 0.81% in BTC terms, so it's losing relative strength. Meanwhile the broader alt set is outpacing the king of crypto, leaving $BTC looking modest by comparison. Nothing wild, just the alts taking the lead while ETH falls a bit behind.

$CBRSB slid to 185.02 USDT, down 7.66% from its recent highs. The tokenized stock barely clung to its low of 184.62 USDT and traded about 1.21 M USDT in volume.

Nvidia's bStock $NVDAB is hanging at 227.96 USDT, a 1.23% dip. It peeked at 232.77 USDT earlier and still pushed roughly 10.96 M USDT through the books.

Tesla's $TSLAB dropped to 350.31 USDT, off 2.55% after touching 359.67 USDT. Volume sat near 5.31 M USDT, showing the usual 24/7 churn.

All three keep moving while the traditional market sleeps, so you can watch the swings any hour. No fireworks, just the usual after-hours action.

$BTC held around $83,414 after a tiny 0.4% pop, peaking at $84,564 and touching $82,900 on the lows. Volume sat near 12.8k, so the move felt light.

$ETH nudged up 0.5% to $2,676, with a high of $2,749 and a low of $2,656. Over 312k coins changed hands, pushing quote volume past $845 M.

$BNB rose 0.6% to $762.77, swung between $750.47 and $769.33, and traded about 123k units, giving roughly $93.6 M in USDT.

All three stayed in a narrow band, so watch the next resistance: $84,600 for $BTC, $2,750 for $ETH and $770 for $BNB. Nothing wild yet, just a steady grind.

$PUMP surged 17.6% to $0.00583, flashing a high of $0.00601 before slipping back to $0.00468. $AAVE jumped 14.1% and is now $166.79, having swung between $145.29 and $176.28. Meanwhile $HBAR fell 14.5% to $0.10369, trading near its low of $0.10278 after peaking at $0.12463. The winners are ripping off double-digit gains, the loser is digging deep into the red. Nothing crazy, just a clear split between the few rockets and the one that got left behind.

$XRP's 24-hour swing sat at about 4.35%, well under its week-average 6.45%, that's roughly a third tighter than usual. It nudged up 0.35% to $1.5178, so the price stayed pretty flat inside that narrowed band.

$SOL moved just a hair, 3.67% range versus a typical 4.34%, basically on the same level as its normal volatility. It inched up 0.108% to $120.06, holding steady through the day.

$SUI's range was 9.57% against an 11.25% average, also close to its regular swing. It slipped 1.684% to $1.1792, staying within that expected window.

All three tokens kept their moves tight enough to stay within the usual limits, nothing wild on the charts.
